subject: Science
stem: For a combustible substance to catch fire and burn, it must first be heated to a minimum temperature at which it spontaneously ignites in the presence of air. This minimum temperature is called the substance's:
explanation: Ignition temperature is the minimum temperature a substance must reach to catch fire — a fire extinguisher works partly by cooling the burning material below this temperature, cutting off one leg of the 'fire triangle' (fuel, heat, oxygen).

subject: Science
stem: This fossil fuel formed over millions of years from the remains of ancient forests and swamp vegetation, buried under layers of sediment and subjected to heat and pressure, and is primarily used to generate electricity in thermal power plants. It is:
explanation: Coal forms from ancient plant matter (vegetation, forests) compressed over geological time — petroleum and natural gas instead form from the remains of ancient marine organisms (plankton) under similar heat and pressure conditions.
